text.p: Usinor Sacilor chairman Francis Mer said on Tuesday that the dividend of three francs set for 1996 was "reasonable" and "responsible".
Usinor cut the dividend from four francs per share in 1995 after reporting a drop in net attributable profit to 1.49 billion francs in 1996 from 4.43 billion earlier on Tuesday.
"The three franc figure is a reasonable and responsible figure," Mer told a news conference.
He and Finance Director Robert Hudry said the dividend was in line with the group's commitment to pay shareholders an average of 25 percent of earnings.

Usinor distributed a 1995 net dividend of four francs on earnings per share (EPS) of 20.9 francs and will pay out three francs for 1996 on EPS of 6.12 francs, for an average payout ratio for the two years of more than 25 percent, Hudry said.
